<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Business and economy'''
*[[China–United States trade war]], [[Censorship of TikTok]]
**[[Carl J. Nichols]], a [[United States federal judge|federal judge]] for the [[United States District Court for the District of Columbia|District Court for the District of Columbia]], blocks the [[United States Department of Commerce|Commerce Department]] from imposing restrictions on [[China]]-based app [[TikTok]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-tiktok-idUSKBN28H30G (Reuters)]
*Swedish furniture giant [[IKEA]] says it will stop printing its famed [[IKEA Catalogue|annual catalogue]], ending a seven-decade tradition as customers move to digital alternatives. [https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2020/12/ikea-to-stop-publishing-catalogue-after-70-years/ (Retail Gazette)]
*[[Israel–United Arab Emirates relations]]
**Sheikh [[Hamad bin Khalifa Al Nahyan]], a member of the Abu Dhabi royal family, purchases a 50% stake in [[Israeli Premier League]] club [[Beitar Jerusalem F.C.]], following the establishment of relations between the two countries this year. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-55229118 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
*****[[Ontario]] reports 1,925 cases, a new single-day record. [http://globalnews.ca/news/7505755/ontario-coronavirus-cases-december-7-covid19/ (Global News)]
****[[Prime Minister of Canada|Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] says that the [[Canada|country]] will receive 240,000 doses of [[Pfizer]] and [[BioNTech]]’s [[BNT162b2|vaccine candidate]] by the end of the year. [https://apnews.com/article/justin-trudeau-canada-coronavirus-pandemic-ace90d898020fe5035c2b605bdb58a5e (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****[[Mayor of the District of Columbia|Mayor]] [[Muriel Bowser]] announces restrictions on high-contact sports amid a rise of cases in the area. However, the restrictions will not apply to professional or university sports. [https://www.npr.org/local/305/2020/12/08/944222094/d-c-mayor-announces-restrictions-on-high-contact-sports-amid-rising-c-o-v-i-d-numbers (NPR)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
*****After the [[Michigan|state]] surpasses 400,000 confirmed cases of COVID-19, [[Governor of Michigan|Governor]] [[Gretchen Whitmer]] extends the statewide partial shutdown on businesses, indoor dining in restaurants, and in-person instruction at high schools and colleges through December 20. [https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2020/12/07/whitmer-administration-covid-pause-to-continue-december-20-pandemic/3858317001/ (''The Detroit News'')] [https://www.clickondetroit.com/health/2020/12/07/michigan-coronavirus-cases-up-to-404386-death-toll-now-at-9947/ (WDIV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wyoming]]
*****[[Wyoming]] Governor [[Mark Gordon (politician)|Mark Gordon]] issues a statewide [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] for indoor public spaces, tighter restrictions on gathering sizes, and a reduction in hours for certain businesses. The mask mandate will go into effect on December 9 and will last until January 8. [https://www.wyomingnews.com/coronavirus/gordon-announces-statewide-mask-mandate-tighter-restrictions-on-gatherings-in-updated-orders/article_255fc460-ef5c-5b7a-ae88-891ff517ed19.html (''Wyoming Tribune Eagle'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]]
****[[Prime Minister of Denmark|Prime Minister]] [[Mette Frederiksen]] announces a tightening of a partial [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] in 38 [[Municipalities of Denmark|municipalities]] across [[Denmark]], including [[Copenhagen]], from December 9 to January 3. [https://www.thelocal.dk/20201207/latest-denmark-announces-partial-covid-19-lockdown-until-2021 (The Local Denmark)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italian Minister of the Interior|Interior Minister]] [[Luciana Lamorgese]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.repubblica.it/politica/2020/12/07/news/coronavirus_ministra_lamorgese_positiva-277405929/amp/ (''La Repubblica'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Prime Minister of Hungary|Prime Minister]] [[Viktor Orbán]] announces that the [[Hungary|country]] will maintain its COVID-19 restrictions until January 11. [https://news.trust.org/item/20201207114447-92fjx (News.trust.org)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Lithuania]]
****The [[Lithuania]]n [[Government of Lithuania|government]] announces that it will tighten and extend the nationwide lockdown until the end of the year. People are advised to leave their homes only for essential reasons, and the education of senior students will be conducted remotely. [https://en.delfi.lt/politics/lithuania-tightens-lockdown.d?id=85929723 (DELFI EN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports a record 203 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 15,103. [https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/turkey-reports-203-daily-covid-19-deaths/news (''Daily Sabah'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****Former [[Vice Governor of Jakarta|vice-governor]] of [[Jakarta]] and former vice-presidential candidate [[Sandiaga Uno]] tests positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5285589/sandiaga-uno-positif-corona (detikNews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****The [[Indian government]] announces that the [[India|country]] will speed up their reviews of vaccines developed by [[Pfizer]] and [[AstraZeneca]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-speeding-up-review-of-pfizer-astra-covid-19-vaccines-government-official/story-b17fSMZzQmLHM56TkN1DCK.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] eases restrictions, allowing larger private and public gatherings, relaxing patron quotas for businesses (including allowing nightclubs to reopen for the first time since the [[pandemic]] began), and relaxing [[face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mask-wearing]] rules. The [[states and territories of Australia|state]] has not reported a COVID-19 case in 37 days. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2020/dec/06/victoria-eases-covid-restrictions-again-as-it-reaches-37-days-without-a-case (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Eluru outbreak]]
**The number of people infected by a mysterious illness in the city of [[Eluru]], [[Andhra Pradesh]], India, increases to more than 400. The majority of those infected are children and young people. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/12/07/asia/india-mystery-illness-intl-hnk-scli/index.html (CNN)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Holy See Press Office|Holy See Press Director]] [[Matteo Bruni]] announces that [[Pope Francis]] will make his first international apostolic visit in 15 months after accepting the invitation of the [[Republic of Iraq]] and the local Catholic Church to visit the Middle Eastern country of Iraq from 5–8 March 2021. [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/pope/news/2020-12/pope-francis-apostolic-journey-iraq-march-2021.html (Vatican News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Islamic Defenders Front]], [[Islam in Indonesia]]
**Six suspected supporters of controversial [[Indonesians|Indonesian]] [[Islamic cleric]] [[Muhammad Rizieq Shihab]] are killed in a clash with [[Indonesian National Police|police]] on a [[Jakarta–Cikampek Toll Road|highway]] near [[Jakarta]]. The incident occurred when a police car was attacked while following a car believed to be carrying supporters of the cleric, resulting in a [[shootout]]. The police have been investigating the cleric for violations of [[Pandemic prevention|health protocols]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] after large gatherings occurred to celebrate his return to the country from [[Exile|self-exile]] in [[Saudi Arabia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-indonesia-security-idUSKBN28H0GY (Reuters)]
*The [[National Football League]] announces an investigation into the [[Washington Football Team]] for allegations of workplace sexual harassment. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/12/07/beth-wilkinson-lawsuit-washington-football/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Hong Kong Autonomy Act]]
**The [[United States Department of the Treasury|US Department of the Treasury]] imposes [[Executive Order 13936|sanctions]] on all 14 [[Vice Chairperson of the National People's Congress|Vice Chairpersons of the National People's Congress]] of [[China]], for "undermining Hong Kong's autonomy and restricting the freedom of expression or assembly." [https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/financial-sanctions/recent-actions/20201207 (US Department of the Treasury)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020 Ghanaian general election]]
**Voters in [[Ghana]] head to the polls to elect their [[President of Ghana|president]] as well as the members of [[Parliament of Ghana|parliament]]. Current president [[Nana Akufo-Addo]] of the [[New Patriotic Party]] is expected to have a tight race with his most promising challenger, [[John Mahama]] of the [[National Democratic Congress (Ghana)|National Democratic Congress]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ghana-election/voting-starts-in-ghana-presidential-and-parliamentary-election-idUSKBN28H0JQ (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Egyptian parliamentary election]]
**The final phase of [[Egypt]]'s latest [[Elections in Egypt|parliamentary election]] begins. The voting process will continue until the end of the next day. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1773886/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
*[[2020 Venezuelan parliamentary election]]
**[[President of Venezuela|President]] [[Nicolás Maduro]]'s [[United Socialist Party of Venezuela]] has reportedly won almost 68% in [[Venezuela]]'s latest parliamentary election. The vote was overshadowed by a boycott of the political opposition led by [[Juan Guaidó]] and a low voter turnout of only 31%. [https://www.dw.com/en/venezuela-maduro-wins-total-control-of-legislature-after-vote/a-55836514 (DW)]
**The [[United States]] refuses to recognize the results, describing the election as a "charade". The [[European Union]] also rejects the legitimacy of the election. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-election-results-idUSKBN28H0L3 (Reuters)] [https://www.voanews.com/americas/us-condemns-venezuela-election-charade (VOA)]
*[[2020 Romanian legislative election]]
**Incumbent [[Prime Minister of Romania|Prime Minister]] [[Ludovic Orban]] resigns after the poor results of his candidacy in the legislative election. He is succeeded ''ad interim'' by [[Ministry of National Defence (Romania)|Minister of National Defence]] [[Nicolae Ciucă]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-55222276 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Belarus at the Olympics]]
**The [[International Olympic Committee]] announces that [[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] and his son [[Viktor Lukashenko|Viktor]] will be banned from all [[Olympic Games]], including the upcoming [[2020 Summer Olympics|Tokyo Games]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/Sports/wireStory/ioc-suspends-belarus-president-lukashenko-olympic-games-74586905 (ABC News)]
*The [[International Olympic Committee]], after an unanimous vote, decides to make competitive breakdancing a sport, and would appear in the [[2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Olympics in]] [[Paris]]. [https://deadline.com/2020/12/olympics-breakdancing-official-sport-paris-2024-games-1234651956/ (Deadline.com)]
